Also excluded: Crimea, DPR, LPR, individual nationals of Cuba, SDN-listed persons, and 'any other country or region restricted by law (this changes occasionally)'. Hand-curated from the help article (not an automated collector).

P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but foreign currency must be surrendered. As a UEMOA member, Côte d'Ivoire applies Regulation 06/2024/CM/UEMOA. Residents must surrender all foreign-currency income received outside the UEMOA or paid by a non-resident to an approved intermediary (art. 5), meaning conversion to CFA francs. Resident economic operators must collect and repatriate all export proceeds for goods and services through an approved intermediary (art. 11).

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024/CM/UEMOA, art. 5
sources.quote: Les résidents sont tenus de céder à un intermédiaire agréé tous les revenus ou produits en devises encaissés en dehors de l'UEMOA ou versés par un non-résident.

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024, art. 11
sources.quote: Les opérateurs économiques résidents sont tenus d'encaisser et de rapatrier dans le pays d’exportation, auprès d'un intermédiaire agréé, l’intégralité des sommes provenant des exportations de biens et services à l’étranger

P1_fx_receipts.notes: Annex II (deadlines/thresholds) not read. Same regime as Senegal (SN.json).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Only with authorisation. Residents opening domestic foreign-currency accounts, or accounts abroad, need prior authorisation from the Minister of Finance after a binding BCEAO opinion (Reg. 06/2024 art. 7).

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024, art. 7
sources.quote: Article 7 : Détention de comptes en devises par les résidents L’ouverture par les résidents de comptes intérieurs en devises ou de comptes à l'étranger est soumise à l'autorisation préalable du Ministre chargé des Finances, après avis conforme de la BCEAO

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Côte D'Ivoire (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

P4_paypal.answer: Limited. Côte d'Ivoire is a listed PayPal market but not on the Payouts list. A 2026 Ivorian guide describes PayPal as 'limited (send only)', with no direct withdrawal to Ivorian banks.

P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: serves Côte d'Ivoire. Freelancers receive platform payouts and withdraw in CFA to an Ivorian bank account, with direct Orange Money/Wave withdrawal reported. L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: the OHADA entreprenant status, a simple declaration of activity for an individual exercising a civil, commercial, craft or agricultural professional activity. In Côte d'Ivoire formalities go through the CEPICI one-stop shop, which also issues the tax existence declaration (DFE) and taxpayer account. Commercial guides cite 24–48 hours and about FCFA 15,000–40,000 for an individual enterprise.

sources.title: AUDCG, art. 30
sources.quote: Art.30.- L’entreprenant est un entrepreneur indi viduel, personne physique qui, sur simple déclaration prévue dans le présent Acte unifo rme, exerce une activité professionnelle civile, commerciale, artisanale ou agricole.

sources.title: Créer son entreprise au CEPICI (2026)
sources.quote: Le guichet unique annonce 24 à 72 heures pour un dossier complet.

L1_registration.notes: CEPICI's own fee schedule not captured; costs are from a commercial blog.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The taxpayer account (compte contribuable), obtained with the tax existence declaration (DFE) through the CEPICI one-stop shop. The DFE is required for investment declarations, and a national ID card or passport copy is part of CEPICI dossiers.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Small businesses are taxed on turnover under the entreprenant regime (Finance Law 2021). The communal tax (TCE) applies at or below FCFA 5m TTC (2.5% for services, 2% for trade, per DGI). The State tax (TEE) applies from FCFA 5,000,001 to 50m at 5% (4% for trade), halved with an approved management centre, and replaces the business licence, profit tax and VAT. Above that, micro-enterprise and real regimes apply. Liberal and non-commercial professions are taxed under BNC, which micro-entrepreneurs may opt into. The treatment of residents' foreign-source income was not established.

sources.title: Le système fiscal ivoirien — régime de l'entreprenant
sources.quote: Le taux de la taxe est fixé à 5 %. Pour les contribuabl es exerçant des activités de commerce ou de négoce, ce taux est ramené à 4 %. Ces taux sont réduits de moitié en cas d’adhésion du contribuable à un Centre de Gestion agréé (CGA).

sources.title: Le système fiscal ivoirien — TEE scope
sources.quote: Cette taxe s e substitue à la patente, à l’impôt sur les bénéfices et à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée.

sources.title: Le système fiscal ivoirien — TCE rates
sources.quote: - 2 % pour les activités de commerce ou de négoce ; - 2,5 % pour les autres types d’activités, y compris les prestations de services.

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: TRAP: Ivoire-Juriste swaps the TCE rates (2.5% trade / 2% services); the DGI document gives 2% trade / 2.5% other incl. services and is used. PwC's Côte d'Ivoire pages returned 404. The DGI document's date was not established.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Entreprenant-regime taxpayers (up to FCFA 50m) do not charge VAT, since the TEE replaces it. For VAT-registered businesses, the tax code treats certain services not used in Côte d'Ivoire, supplied to companies without a local establishment, as exports. Since Finance Law 2024, services of online platform operators are excluded from that export treatment.

sources.title: TEE replaces VAT

sources.title: Côte d'Ivoire : nouveautés de l'ordonnance 2023-719 et de la LF 2024

L4_vat_gst.notes: The standard VAT rate (18% in UEMOA practice) was not captured from a Côte d'Ivoire source; not stated as a fact.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 2013-450 on personal data, with ARTCI as the protection authority. Processing must be declared to ARTCI, or authorised for sensitive categories such as biometrics. ARTCI has asked public and private bodies to declare customer files, direct marketing (SMS/email) and biometric systems.

sources.title: ARTCI – Le traitement des données personnelles désormais soumis à une autorisation préalable
sources.quote: Dans cette perspective, l’Autorité de régulation demande aux responsables des organismes publics et privés de procéder dans les meilleurs délais auprès de ses services aux déclarations des traitements portant sur les données telles que les fichiers ou les bases de données (personnels, clientèles, usagers, patients, abonnés, élèves ou étudiants, etc.), le marketing direct (SMS, courrier électronique, etc.) et les systèmes biométriques (photos, empruntes digitales, ADN, etc.)

sources.title: Côte d’Ivoire : L’ARTCI met en garde contre les prêts en ligne (Aug 2023)
sources.quote: L’article 5 de cette loi stipule clairement que « le traitement des données à caractère personnel est soumis à une déclaration préalable auprès de l’ Autorité de protection des données ».

L5_data_protection.notes: Law 2013-450 and Decree 2015-79 texts not read; art. 5 quoted via Digital Business Africa.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Not verified. A Digital Mag article quotes an 'article 11' giving buyers in distance and off-premises sales 10 working days from delivery to return a product for exchange or refund (return costs aside), extended to 3 months if the seller's mandatory information is missing. Articles 11–12 of the e-commerce law 2013-546 (official text) cover promotions and fraud penalties, so the rule must come from the consumer law 2016-412, whose text could not be retrieved.
L6_consumer_ecommerce.note: Searched 2026-10-18: 'Côte d'Ivoire loi 2013-546 transactions électroniques droit de rétractation', 'loi n° 2016-412 relative à la consommation vente à distance délai de rétractation', '"dix jours ouvrables" "vente à distance" Côte d'Ivoire'. Read: official Law 2013-546 (SHERLOC), whose arts. 11–12 do not contain the rule; Digital Mag (press). CIVLII copies of Law 2016-412 returned 404 (script and browser).

sources.title: Commerce électronique / Consommer en ligne sans se faire piéger
sources.quote: L’article 11 prévoit que « pour toutes les opérations de vente à distance ou de vente hors établissement, l’acheteur d’un produit dispose d’un délai de dix jours ouvrables, à compter de la livraison de sa commande, pour faire retour de ce produit au vendeur pour échange ou remboursement, sans pénalités, à l’exception des frais de retour ».

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) Entreprenant turnover taxes (TCE ≤ FCFA 5m; TEE 5% up to FCFA 50m, halved via an approved management centre), replacing profit tax, the business licence and VAT (L3). (2) Paystack Starter accounts for unregistered individuals (P3). (3) Export treatment for qualifying services not used in Côte d'Ivoire (L4; excludes online platform operators since 2024). 2026 Finance Law (Deloitte): labelled digital startups operating outside the ZBTIC free zone are exempt for three years after labelling from profit tax, the micro-enterprise tax or the taxe d'État de l'Entreprenant. The entreprenant taxes themselves remain in the 2026 law.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Card payments on your own site through Paystack (a Stripe company). Stripe lists this country under its extended network. (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
